subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in TUI observe/mirror mode that can display activity across channel and session boundaries, or keep TUI visibility limited to explicitly selected sessions plus logs?
rationale: The requested behavior changes transcript visibility and likely adds public CLI or config surface, so automation cannot choose the security and product boundary safely.

options.title: Design scoped observe mode
options.body: Add read-only observation only after maintainers define session/channel scope, authorization, and audit semantics.

options.title: Limit to selected-session live-tail
options.body: Keep broader mirroring out of scope and let the existing PR path fix only live updates for the selected session.

options.title: Decline cross-channel visibility
options.body: Document `openclaw logs --follow` and explicit `--session` selection as the supported monitoring paths.

recommendation.title: Design scoped observe mode
recommendation.body: Add read-only observation only after maintainers define session/channel scope, authorization, and audit semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the isolation behavior and is the strongest history signal for deciding whether TUI should regain any cross-channel visibility as an explicit product mode.
